text: Granada fell to the Catholic Monarchs, ending the Reconquista and freeing the Crown to fund an Atlantic voyage
The Capitulations of Santa Fe granted Columbus the titles of Admiral and Viceroy of any lands he might find
Columbus sailed from Palos de la Frontera with the Niña, the Pinta and the Santa María
Landfall at Guanahaní, named San Salvador and claimed for Castile
The ships reached the coast of Cuba, which Columbus took for the Asian mainland
Columbus sighted the island he named La Española, later Hispaniola
The Santa María ran aground on Christmas night and her timbers were used to raise Fort La Navidad, the first Spanish settlement in the Americas
Spaniards and Ciguayo warriors clashed at Samaná Bay, the first armed fight between the two worlds
Columbus was received in Barcelona by Isabella and Ferdinand and paraded the gold, parrots and captives he had brought back
Pope Alexander VI issued the bull Inter caetera, granting Castile the lands west of a line drawn through the Atlantic
The second voyage sailed from Cádiz with seventeen ships carrying settlers, horses and livestock
The fleet claimed the island of San Juan Bautista, today Puerto Rico
Columbus returned to La Navidad to find the fort burned and its whole garrison dead
La Isabela was founded on the north coast of Hispaniola, the first planned Spanish town in the New World
Fort Santo Tomás was raised in the Cibao valley to hold the goldfields inland
The Treaty of Tordesillas divided the unclaimed world between Castile and Portugal along a meridian in the Atlantic
Spanish cavalry and arquebuses broke the massed Taíno host at the Battle of Vega Real
Bartholomew Columbus founded Santo Domingo, the oldest lasting European city in the Americas
The third voyage reached the Paria peninsula, the first Spanish landing on the American mainland
Francisco de Bobadilla seized the government of Hispaniola and shipped Columbus back to Spain in chains
